summary: Streaming responses: suspected under-counting of output tokens in usage/metering (customer reports mismatch vs non-streaming)
description:
Customer: PromptForge (self-serve)

Issue summary
- Customer reports that Redwood usage data appears to under-count output tokens for streaming responses (SSE). Their internal tokenization (tiktoken equivalent for the model family) and transcript length suggests materially more output tokens than Redwood-reported output tokens.
- They state that non-streaming requests appear to match expectations more closely.

Customer impact
- PromptForge uses output token counts to validate spend and to monitor prompt changes. Undercounting makes their internal dashboards unreliable and creates confusion (they believe Redwood may be dropping tokens or misreporting usage).
- No claim of over-billing; customer concern is accuracy/consistency. (If confirmed, this would be under-metering on our side.)

Environment
- Prod
- Regions observed: us-east primarily; one example from eu-west
- Models: llama-3.1-70b-instruct and mixtral-8x7b-instruct

Reported symptoms
- For streaming calls, Redwood usage.output_tokens (or equivalent usage output field in response/usage export) is lower than expected by ~20–40%.
- Customer provided examples where the visible streamed text length is stable, but usage shows fewer output tokens.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided)
1) Call chat/completions with stream=true
2) Consume SSE events until [DONE]
3) Compare Redwood-reported output tokens vs internal tokenization of concatenated deltas

Example request details (sanitized)
- Request IDs:
  - rq_9d7f7d3c3b0f4d8a (2025-02-21 15:12Z, us-east, llama-3.1-70b-instruct)
  - rq_2a1c1c0b1e6a4a23 (2025-02-20 19:44Z, eu-west, mixtral-8x7b-instruct)
- Client: Python SDK 0.18.x (customer claims)
- Streaming: enabled

Expected
- Streaming and non-streaming paths should produce equivalent output token counts for the same generated content (within any known tokenizer/version differences we document).

Actual
- Streaming path appears to emit a smaller output token total than content indicates.

Initial hypothesis
- Streaming code path emits token metering increments inconsistently (e.g., missing final flush, disconnect path not counted, or only counting a subset of deltas).

References
- Related Slack triage thread: sources/slack/eng-platform/1737849033-output-token-metering-streaming-bug.json
- This is relevant to internal Unit Economics metric correctness; output token parity is a prerequisite for blended $/1M output tokens reporting.
comments:
2025-02-21 16:08Z — Reporter (Nadia Rahman)
Created ticket from support escalation + telemetry triage. PromptForge sent multiple request IDs showing streaming output token totals lower than expected. Assigning to Data Quality / Metering for confirmation and scoping.

Next steps:
- Validate raw metering events for provided request IDs
- Compare streaming vs non-streaming token attribution for same model/version
- Determine if billing exports / usage API also affected or only response-level usage fields.

2025-02-21 16:33Z — Assignee (Caleb Johnson)
Pulled metering traces for rq_9d7f7d3c3b0f4d8a. Confirmed discrepancy: streaming event stream shows N chunks, but usage aggregation is missing a final increment. Looks consistent with “finalization” not firing when stream completes.

Not seeing evidence of dropped generation; only metering undercount.

Looping in Token Metering owner + gateway eng.
CC: Logan Wright, Chloe Martin.

2025-02-21 17:05Z — Logan Wright
Confirmed similar pattern in warehouse rollups for a small slice of streaming traffic: output_tokens lower vs expected decode steps, especially for longer generations. This aligns with earlier internal notes about streaming parity.

This appears to be in the gateway/streaming accounting path, not the model runtime.

Linking ongoing triage thread: sources/slack/eng-platform/1737849033-output-token-metering-streaming-bug.json

2025-02-21 18:22Z — Chloe Martin
Found bug in streaming response handler: when the stream terminates, we weren’t consistently emitting the final “usage_summary” event for all code paths (normal completion vs tool-call vs early client disconnect). For normal completion, finalization could be skipped if the writer closed before callback ran.

Fix in progress; likely a hotfix PR.

Tentative fix approach:
- Emit periodic metering increments per chunk (or per N tokens) and guarantee final flush in a finally{} block
- Add regression tests for stream completion and disconnect paths

2025-02-22 00:41Z — Nadia Rahman
Hotfix PR opened: sources/github/redwood/pr-19355-streaming-output-token-metering-fix.json

Plan:
- Merge + deploy to prod under expedited process
- Validate parity via canary + comparison query (streaming vs non-streaming cohorts)
- After deploy, re-check customer request IDs (new traffic) and provide customer-facing update

Note: For historical requests, we may not be able to reconstruct exact output tokens if the per-chunk increments were never emitted. We can confirm scope and provide guidance on time window impacted.

2025-02-22 09:18Z — Sean Gallagher
SRE: Approved hotfix rollout. Monitoring error rates + metering ingestion. Please ensure cardinality unaffected.

Also adding a canary check PR to catch future regressions: sources/github/perf-canary/pr-455-add-canary-check-for-output-token-metering.json

2025-02-22 14:37Z — Caleb Johnson
Post-deploy validation (prod us-east):
- Compared streaming vs non-streaming outputs in controlled replay: output token counts now within ~1–2% (expected variance due to tokenizer edge cases).
- Confirmed that the “final usage flush” event is emitted on normal completion and tool-call completion paths.
- Client disconnect path now emits usage up to last chunk; still expected that abrupt disconnect mid-stream reflects partial generation delivered.

Marking as resolved pending customer confirmation.

2025-02-24 17:12Z — Support (Nadia Rahman)
Customer update sent to PromptForge:
- We identified and fixed an output-token metering bug affecting a subset of streaming responses.
- Fix deployed 2025-02-22.
- New streaming requests should now match non-streaming usage more closely.

Asked customer to re-test and share any remaining discrepant request IDs.

2025-02-25 10:29Z — Support (Nadia Rahman)
Customer confirmed new requests match expectations; remaining mismatch they saw was from pre-fix requests. They are OK with no retroactive changes and mainly needed correctness going forward.

Closing ticket.

Follow-ups (internal):
- Keep canary check enabled for streaming output token parity
- Add this scenario to oncall playbook for unit economics discrepancies (metering parity checks)
- Consider annotation in internal dashboards for known impacted date window (2025-02-18 to 2025-02-22) if finance asks
resolution: Root cause: streaming response handler did not reliably emit final output-token usage flush across all completion paths, leading to under-counted output_tokens for some streaming requests. Fix deployed via hotfix PR (pr-19355) on 2025-02-22; added canary guardrail (perf-canary pr-455). Customer validated post-fix behavior; ticket closed.
